positive_feedback: shared.rs (HIR) is the cleanest new module in this diff: pure data types, no codegen dependency, mirrors buffer.rs/subgroup.rs discipline exactly; comprehensive inline tests including Bool-rejection, all-numeric acceptance, SharedId ordering

codegen/shared.rs documents the ONE-vs-TWO index arity distinction prominently at the top of the file — this is the most critical correctness invariant and it is impossible to miss; comment references AT-1615 for the dedup story

OQ1 SET-based analysis is both sound and documented: the r3 changelog rationale (multi-slot self-write `tile[0]=a; tile[1]=b; let w=tile[0];` is silent) is captured in a DESIGN.md paragraph, in typecheck.rs field comments, and in AT-1636(b) test — the three-source documentation makes the zero-false-positive claim auditable
AT-429 inversion is handled correctly: the test is renamed (not just the assertion changed), and the comment explains why the OQ2 policy supersedes the prior CRITICAL-4 exception

Capability emission for F16 shared arrays is explicitly handled in emit_shared_globals with a comment calling out that observe_type does NOT cover F16 — prevents a class of silent missing-capability bugs from future maintainers
The double-counted aggregate shared memory check (typecheck + validate) is conservative rather than under-counting; duplicating a compile error is low-severity vs missing one
All 5 existing callers of prepare_kernel_checked (resident_timing.rs x2, resident_matmul.rs x4, dispatch_shared_m32.rs) are updated to pass meta.shared_memory_bytes — no partial migration
BTreeMap used throughout shared module (SharedBindings, shared_write_sets, shared_name_map) — consistent with AT-227 no-HashMap policy
Bench AT-1623 removal with explanatory comment is the right call — shipping TFLOPS for a kernel that computes zeros would have been a trust violation against benchmarking integrity

minor_issues.description: Aggregate shared-memory size check runs in both typecheck_kernel_body (TypecheckError::SharedMemoryTooLarge) and validate.rs (HirError::SharedMemoryTooLarge). A kernel with >65536 bytes will report the error twice to the user. Not a correctness problem (both copies say the same thing), but cosmetically noisy. Suggest: skip the validate.rs check if typecheck already populates shared_decls, or fold one into the other in M3.3.

AT-1636(d) ends with `let _any_warn = ...;` and a comment 'Don't assert strictly'. The test verifies the hard error does NOT fire but does not assert the advisory warning fires. This is a known conservative choice given binding-id tracking uncertainty. A follow-up in M3.3 with a more deterministic undecidable-index fixture would tighten this.

find_mul_add_in_expr returns None for SharedRead (line 603-605) without recursing into the index sub-expression. This is conservative (SharedRead.index cannot contain coopmat_mul_add in the current type system), but the comment acknowledges this: 'scan it for completeness (unlikely to contain coopmat_mul_add)'. The current behavior is safe; a future kernel with a complex index expression that happens to call coopmat_mul_add would silently suppress the check. Low risk given type constraints, but worth a TODO note.

elem_byte_size() uses panic! for unsupported bit widths (the _ arm). This is the only panic in new lib code. It is properly documented and cannot be reached via well-typed HIR (Bool is rejected by is_allowed_shared_element), but differs from the Result-returning error style elsewhere. Could return a BodyCodegenError in a future cleanup pass.

summary: M3.2 (re-scoped to shared[T,N] language feature) is a high-quality, merge-ready implementation. The shared[T,N] pipeline is clean end-to-end. OQ1 (set-based missing-barrier) and OQ2 (divergent-barrier) analyses match the r3 design precisely. The honest deferral of the four compute-zeros GPU tests and the TFLOPS bench removal are the right calls and are executed correctly. Metadata v3 back-compat, coopmat-from-shared wiring, and the runtime preflight addition are all correct and additive. Four minor non-blocking issues are noted for M3.3 cleanup.
